standard_prerequisites.name: The integral closure of a ring in a product of rings is the product of the integral closures in the factors, via the idempotents of the product
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the algebraic fact that the proof invokes and sketches.

standard_prerequisites.use: Is the key observation that forces the integral closure inside a product to be a product.

core_obligations: Translate to algebra: the normalization is defined through integral closures, so over an affine chart the claim becomes the statement that for a ring map A to B with B a product of two rings, the integral closure of A in B is the product of the integral closures of A in the two factors (proof lines 14320-14323).

Use the idempotents: the two standard idempotents of the product are integral over A, hence lie in the integral closure of A in B, which forces that closure to be a product of two rings (proof lines 14324-14327).

Identify the factors: the two factors obtained in this way are the integral closures of A in the two component rings, which is the algebraic form of the claim, so the normalization over the disjoint union is the disjoint union of the normalizations (proof lines 14327-14330).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the statement about integral closures in a product of rings (proof lines 14320-14323).
Show that the idempotents are integral and hence force the integral closure to split, with factors the individual integral closures (proof lines 14324-14330).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that the normalization of the base in a disjoint union of two schemes is the disjoint union of the normalizations in the two pieces (statement lines 14312-14318). The counted proof reduces the geometric statement to the algebraic statement about the integral closure of a ring in a product of rings, and then gives the key reason why the statement holds, namely that the standard idempotents of the product are integral over the base ring and hence belong to the integral closure, which forces it to be a product whose factors are the individual integral closures (proof lines 14320-14330). It is H2: the reduction and the decisive observation are in the counted span; the author explicitly leaves 'some details' to the reader at the end, and what is left there is the routine identification of the two factors, not the mechanism of the proof.
